Subject: Bundled purchase question — revenue split and lead protection

Hi Aditya / Diego,

We're close to committing to Redwood for a pilot (roughly $120k list for 12 months) but the procurement team asked for clarity on how commissions and lead credits will work when BlueMarsh resells a bundled package that includes Redwood seats + implementation from our systems integrator (ImplWorks). Specifically:

- How does Redwood calculate commission when the buyer pays one invoice to BlueMarsh that covers both product and services?
- Is there a protected lead / registration window so we retain credit if a prospect signs within X months?
- Any carve-outs for implementation services (we usually keep services margin) or do you expect a pooled revenue split?

If you can send a one-page table and a sample SOW attachment that shows how the split is documented, that would help procurement. Tom Rivera from ImplWorks is on copy — he may have preferred contract language for services.

Ellen — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: we support a negotiated waterfall that preserves reseller lead credit while enabling implementation partners to keep services margin. Details below and I attached a draft commission waterfall table + example SOW that we use internally.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Product commission to reseller: 15% of product ARR (standard registered-reseller rate for BlueMarsh)
- Implementation partner carve: implementation services are out of scope for product commission unless Redwood is directly invoiced for services; in that case we suggest a 50/50 split of the services margin above cost (example in worksheet)
- Deal-level blended credit: when BlueMarsh invoices the customer for bundled product+services, product revenue is first isolated (per SOW line items) and commission paid on that amount
- Lead protection: 9-month registration window from first qualified meeting date; retro credits for referrals closed within that window if not claimed by another partner

Action items: 1) Diego — can you validate the 15% baseline and the 9-month window against current partner T&Cs? 2) Monica — can you review the SOW template and call out any procurement flags?

I attached: proposed-commission-waterfall.xlsx, SOW-implementation-split.docx

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with you + Tom to walk through the table.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — quick notes after reviewing the worksheet:

- Product isolation is key: procurement often wants a single invoice. We must ensure the SOW line items enumerate product SKUs and services separately so accounting can allocate revenue correctly.
- 15% reseller commission aligns with current tiers, but suggest we add a ladder: 12% for <$50k ARR, 15% for $50k-$250k, 18% for >$250k to incentivize larger deals (BlueMarsh pilot sits in mid-tier).
- Lead protection window: 9 months is customer-friendly. For enterprise deals we sometimes extend to 12 months; propose default 9 months, extendable on a per-deal basis with partner manager sign-off.
- Clawbacks: propose 180-day clawback for refunds/credits on invoiced product revenue. If procurement requires no clawbacks, we need a commercial exception approved by Sales Ops (Monica).

I'll update the spreadsheet with the tiered percentages and the clawback row and re-upload.

Diego
Head of Partner Operations | Redwood Inference

Ellen / Tom — quick confirmation and final language below that Sales Ops can add to the reseller addendum. If that works I'll ask Legal to insert into the draft contract:

1) Invoicing: Redwood accepts a consolidated BlueMarsh invoice that lists product and services as separate line items (product SKU / quantity / unit price; services description / hours / rate) — product revenue will be used to compute reseller commission.

2) Subcontractors & services billing: ImplWorks may invoice BlueMarsh directly for implementation services and retain services margin. Redwood does not require services revenue to flow through BlueMarsh for commission to be paid, provided BlueMarsh provides a signed SOW that ties product units to the customer purchase and confirms partner referral for the product portion.

3) Lead protection & clawbacks: Standard lead protection is 9 months from qualified meeting date; 180-day clawback applies to product refunds/credits unless waived in writing. Exceptions require Partner Manager + Sales Ops approval.

4) Tiered commission: 12% (<$50k ARR), 15% ($50k-$250k), 18% (>$250k) for registered deals.

I'll circulate a short addendum and the updated worksheet for Ellen's procurement team. If PO is ready we can accept via DocuSign link.
